traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements in docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md are implemented and verified:
- Core functionality: The `valid-annotation-format` rule supports configurable patterns via both nested (`story.pattern`, `req.pattern`) and flat (`storyPathPattern`, `requirementIdPattern`) options, wired through `ResolvedAnnotationOptions` and used by the validators. - Backward compatibility: When no options are supplied or patterns/examples are omitted, the rule falls back to the original hardcoded defaults (`docs/stories/... .story.md` and `REQ-...`), and pre-existing tests for Story 005.0 continue to pass. - Pattern validation: Regex patterns are compiled with protection against invalid sources; configuration errors are recorded via `buildInvalidRegexError(...)`, surfaced as `invalidRuleConfiguration` diagnostics, and default patterns remain in effect. Tests explicitly assert both the error messages and continued validation behavior. - Error messages & examples: Optional `story.example`/`storyPathExample` and `req.example`/`requirementIdExample` are resolved with correct precedence and injected into `buildStoryErrorMessage` / `buildReqErrorMessage`. Tests cover both custom examples and nested-over-flat precedence, and user docs describe these options clearly. - Schema & quality standards: `getRuleSchema()` defines a strict JSON schema for the rule’s options, with typed properties and `additionalProperties: false` at all levels, and it is attached to `meta.schema`, matching ESLint best practices. - Integration consistency: Default story patterns (`docs/stories/... .story.md`) align with the `valid-story-reference` rule’s default `storyDirectories` and extension handling. Custom patterns affect only format validation; `valid-story-reference` continues to use its own `storyDirectories` configuration, so the rules operate together without conflict. - Documentation: The user-facing API reference documents `storyPathPattern`, `requirementIdPattern`, `storyPathExample`, and `requirementIdExample`, explains defaults, precedence, error behavior, and typical customization scenarios (alternate directories, different ID schemes). Combined with the internal story examples and comprehensive tests, the configuration usage is clearly communicated.
Given the concrete implementation, targeted tests tied to this story, passing full test suite, and aligned documentation, this story is fully implemented and validated.
